description: SOC tests of 7_cell_2000mAh, run by soc_simulate.py: estimation, rest and full-charge corrections, capacity learning and the temperature model. Every test runs from a reboot; expect holds its pass conditions.

discharge.description: SOC estimation while discharging: rest, constant, resistor, pulse, sine and random load, rest, then a long constant discharge. The internal SOC must follow the true SOC.

charge.description: SOC estimation while charging: CC/CV from 5 % to full, then rest. The internal SOC must follow the true SOC.

high_current_discharge.description: High current discharge: 15 A (7.5 C, just below the 16 A slow discharge OCP) from 100 % until the weakest cell reaches 2800 mV under load (above UVP 2700 mV, so no protection trips). At 15 A the voltage drop on the cell resistance ends this at about 40 % SOC, so the discharge goes on at 8 A down to 2800 mV, which leaves about 4 %, then a 40 min rest. (Lower currents are not used: the model's OCV is flat below 0 %, so the simulated cells would run below 0 %.) The internal SOC must follow the true SOC all the way down.

profile.note: 8 A down to 2800 mV, about 4 % left

rest_correction.description: Rest correction: the board starts 10 % too high. After a short discharge a 40 min rest lets the OCV correct the internal SOC (shown SOC holds), then a discharge down to about 4 % spreads the gap: the shown SOC meets the true SOC on the way down.

profile.note: rest: internal SOC corrected from the OCV
discharge to about 4 %, shown SOC catches up

full_charge.description: Full charge: the cell voltages reach the board 50 mV low, so its SOC runs low all through the charge. CC/CV ends at 50 mA, below charging_term_current (100 mA), so the full-charge detection fires: expect the shown SOC of all cells to jump from about 98 to 100 % near the end of charge and stay there in the rest after it.

capacity_learning.description: Capacity learning: the cells are 5 % smaller than the board's capacity_ah. Six cycles between about 90 and 30 % SOC with 40 min rests give the learning points; expect the capacity to move toward the real value at every update, q_nom_ah and SOH to follow, and about one cycle counted per 1.8 Ah discharged.

temperature.description: Temperature model: the whole test runs at 0 degC, the model tables are from 25 degC. The simulated cells have about 3 x the resistance of the tables. With the board's temperature model on, the internal SOC follows the true SOC during the 2 A discharge; remaining capacity (0x94) is the shown SOC x capacity x 0.9 (q_temp_factor at 0 degC). Compare with soc_temperature_off.

profile.note: short rest, remaining capacity read at 0 degC

temperature_off.description: Same as soc_temperature, but the board's temperature model is off (ea_* = 0): the board uses the 25 degC tables at 0 degC, so its internal SOC drifts away from the true SOC during the discharge.

profile.note: short rest, remaining capacity read at 0 degC
